title: An effective versal formal object algebraizes to a versal finite type family
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a category fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes [def-pc-scheme], meaning that cartesian pullbacks exist along every base morphism and each fibre is a groupoid. A local ring has a unique maximal ideal; an Artinian ring satisfies the descending chain condition on ideals. Let $k$ be a field of finite type over $R$ [def-weil-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $s\in S$ be its image. Suppose $R_s$, the localization at the prime corresponding to $s$, is a G-ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-pbc-g-ring]. Suppose $\mathcal X$ preserves directed affine limits on objects: every object over $\varprojlim_i T_i$ for a small directed inverse system of affine $S$-schemes is isomorphic to pullback of an object at some stage. A formal object over a complete Noetherian local $R$-algebra $(C,\mathfrak m)$ with residue field identified with $k$ is a system $\xi_n\in\mathcal X(C/\mathfrak m^n)$, $n\geq1$, with compatible transition isomorphisms; completeness means $C\cong\varprojlim_n C/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Such a system is versal if, for every surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with residue field identified with $k$, every local $R$-map $C\to B$ inducing the identity on $k$, every $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and every isomorphism $z|_B\cong\xi_B$ compatible with the specified identifications over $k$, there exist a local $R$-lift $C\to B'$ and an isomorphism $z\cong\xi_{B'}$ extending the prescribed isomorphism. Here $\xi_B$ denotes pullback from $\xi_n$ for any $n$ with $\mathfrak m^n$ mapping to zero in $B$, and similarly for $B'$. Let $(\xi_n)$ be such a versal formal object. Assume it is effective: there exist $x_C\in\mathcal X(C)$ and isomorphisms $x_C|_{C/\mathfrak m^n}\cong\xi_n$ compatible with all transitions. A point $v$ of an $S$-scheme $V$ is a finite type point if $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is of finite type [def-weil-residue-field, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $V$ locally of finite type over $S$ and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$, say that $y$ is versal at a finite type point $v$ if, for every surjection $B'\to B$ of Artinian local $R$-algebras with residue field identified with $\kappa(v)$, every $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$ restricting to the canonical point $v$, every $z\in\mathcal X(B')$, and every isomorphism $z|_B\cong a^*y$, there exist a lift $a':\operatorname{Spec}B'\to V$ of $a$ and an isomorphism $z\cong(a')^*y$ extending the prescribed isomorphism. Then there exist a finite type $S$-scheme $V$, a finite type point $v\in V$, an $R$-isomorphism $\kappa(v)\cong k$, and $y\in\mathcal X(V)$ such that $y$ is versal at $v$ and $y|_v\cong\xi_1$ under that residue-field isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07XH (lemma-approximate-versal), with Tag 07XF (definition-versal) and definition-versal-formal-object. Only the residue-field and versality conclusions of the approximation lemma are asserted.

proof.text: Choose the effective object $x_C$ supplied in the hypotheses. Apply [lem-sfb-artin-object-graded-approximation] with $N=2$ to obtain $A,\mathfrak n,y,e_2$ and the graded isomorphism. The hypotheses are precisely the given Noetherian base, complete local ring, finite type residue field, G-ring at its image and preservation of directed affine limits on objects. The given effectivity isomorphism identifies $x_C$ modulo $\mathfrak m^2$ with $\xi_2$, so the approximation identifies $y$ modulo $\mathfrak n^2$ with $\xi_2$.

source.place: Tag 07XH (lemma-approximate-versal), first two sentences; Tag 07XB with N=2.

proof.text: The algebra $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]. Put $L=A_{\mathfrak n}$, which is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian], and let $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak nL$. For $t\notin\mathfrak n$ choose $u$ with $tu=1$ modulo $\mathfrak n$; modulo $\mathfrak n^r$, the inverse of $tu=1+h$ is $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(-h)^i$. Thus localization induces $A/\mathfrak n^r\cong L/\mathfrak q^r$ for every $r\geq1$. Set $D=\widehat L$ and $\mathfrak d=\mathfrak qD$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal] and [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power], $D$ is complete Noetherian local, its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak d$, its residue field is $k$, and $D/\mathfrak d^r\cong A/\mathfrak n^r$ canonically for every $r\geq1$. Taking kernels of the adjacent quotient maps gives $\mathfrak d^r/\mathfrak d^{r+1}\cong\mathfrak n^r/\mathfrak n^{r+1}$ compatibly with multiplication. Let $\eta_r=y|_{D/\mathfrak d^r}$.

source.place: Tags 0316, 05GI, 05GG; artin.tex Tag 07XH, definition of eta over the completion.

proof.text: Construct compatible local $R$-maps $f_r:C\to D/\mathfrak d^r$ and isomorphisms $\theta_r:(\xi)_{f_r}\cong\eta_r$. Start at $r=2$ using $e_2$ and the object isomorphism of step 1, and obtain $r=1$ by reduction. Suppose $(f_r,\theta_r)$ has been chosen for $r\geq2$. Both $D/\mathfrak d^{r+1}$ and $D/\mathfrak d^r$ are Artinian local with residue $k$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local]. Apply the stipulated versal lifting property of $\xi$ to their quotient surjection, to $f_r$, to $z=\eta_{r+1}$, and to $\theta_r^{-1}:z|_{D/\mathfrak d^r}\cong(\xi)_{f_r}$. It gives $f_{r+1}$ lifting $f_r$ and, after inversion, $\theta_{r+1}$ reducing to $\theta_r$. Recursion produces the compatible system. This uses only the definition of versality once at each stage; no assertion of algebraization follows from approximation alone.

source.place: Tag 07XH, successive lifts to eta_3, eta_4, ...; formal-defos.tex remark-versal-object.

proof.text: Define $f:C\to D=\varprojlim_rD/\mathfrak d^r$ by $f(c)=(f_r(c))_r$, using completeness [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Each $f_r$ is an $R$-map, so componentwise operations make $f$ an $R$-map; its reduction to $k$ is the identity, hence $f$ is local. Its reduction modulo the square of the maximal ideal is $e_2$, so its cotangent map is surjective. Step 1 and step 2 give equal dimensions of all maximal-ideal graded pieces of $C$ and $D$. Apply [lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-graded-rigidity]: $f$ is an isomorphism. Its inverse is also an $R$-map. The compatible $\theta_r$ identify the formal pullback of $\xi$ along $f$ with $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 07XH, surjectivity and equal graded dimensions imply that the dotted ring map is an isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and let $v$ correspond to $\mathfrak n$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since $A$ is generated by finitely many elements over $R$, $V\to S$ is finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Since $A\to A/\mathfrak n$ is surjective, the canonical point map $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(v)\to V$ is finite type (one affine chart with no algebra generators). Thus $v$ is a finite type point, and $\kappa(v)=A/\mathfrak n\cong k$. To verify versality, take any test $B'\twoheadrightarrow B$, $a:\operatorname{Spec}B\to V$, $z$, and prescribed object isomorphism from the statement. The map $A\to B$ sends $A\setminus\mathfrak n$ to units and extends uniquely to a local map $L\to B$. By [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], some power of the maximal ideal of $B$ vanishes. Consequently $L\to B$ kills $\mathfrak q^r$ for some $r$, and the quotient isomorphisms of step 2 extend it uniquely to $g:D\to B$. Uniqueness follows because every local map $D\to B$ factors through such a quotient.

source.place: Tag 0CXK (lemma-versality-matches), Artinian-valued points are maps from the completed local ring; Tag 07XH, final sentence.

proof.text: Compose $g$ with $f$ to get $C\to B$. Because $B$ is Artinian, the compatible $\theta_r$ of step 3 identify $(\xi)_{g f}$ with $a^*y$: choose $r$ killing the maximal ideal of $B$ and pull back $\theta_r$. They turn the prescribed isomorphism $z|_B\cong a^*y$ into the datum for versality of $\xi$. Obtain a lift $h:C\to B'$ and an isomorphism $z\cong(\xi)_h$ extending it. Define the lifted point by the ring map $A\to D\xrightarrow{f^{-1}}C\xrightarrow{h}B'$. Its reduction is $A\to D\xrightarrow{g}B$, as required. The maximal ideal of $B'$ is nilpotent by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-noetherian-nilpotent], so pulling back some $\theta_r$ identifies $(\xi)_h$ with the pullback of $y$ along this lifted point. Compatibility of the $\theta_r$ ensures that the resulting isomorphism restricts to the prescribed one over $B$. This proves versality at $v$. At $r=1$, $\theta_1$ gives $y|_v\cong\xi_1$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q07-8a8679522 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the delivery against Stacks artin.tex 07XB (lemma-approximate), 07XH (lemma-approximate-versal and its proof) and definition-versal-formal-object, and formal-defos.tex 06GZ. The item statement is byte-identical to live and matches 07XH on an affine Noetherian base. Step 1 applies the new 07XB node with N=2; all its hypotheses are present in the item. Step 2 gets D/d^r = L/q^r and D complete Noetherian local from the cited nodes: completion-noetherian, local-completion-local-ring, mod-ideal (1) for completeness and mod-power (kernel q^r D); each says what is used. Step 3 is the dotted-arrow recursion from the item's own versality hypothesis on the Artinian quotients from noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local; I checked the orientation of theta_r and that each choice extends the previous one. Step 4: f_2 is an iso mod squares; equal graded dimensions come from the 07XB graded iso plus step 2, with matching k-structures through e_2; the rigidity node then makes f an isomorphism. Steps 5-6 are the lifting diagram chase. Nilpotence of m_B and m_B' factors maps through D/d^r. The lift A->D->C->B' reduces to a, and compatibility of the theta_r extends the prescribed iso; theta_1 gives y|_v = xi_1. New node object-graded-approximation is 07XB (1)-(6) on an affine base, matching hypothesis by hypothesis, with no versality content. New node complete-local-cotangent-graded-rigidity is true by my own proof: Nakayama plus complete Nakayama give surjectivity, and equal lengths of C/m^j and D/n^j give injectivity. I tested it on k[[t]]->k[[t]]/(t^2), Z_p->F_p, Z_p[[t]]->Z_p and the identity. It is not a duplicate of lem-sfb-complete-local-cotangent-surjectivity, which needs k-algebras and states surjectivity only; the item works over an arbitrary Noetherian R. A rg -L search for duplicates over the snapshot found none (07XB/07XH/06GZ/0CXK tags, approximation and complete-local names, gradings). I accept the tool_use lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian. There are no SGA citations, and live and side-live still show the item unsplit. No fixes written.
